activity.notes: Reviewed seed Activity used only to mint the distinct 1868–1947 imperial-era Japanese state identity. 'Imperial Japan (1868–1947) / 일본 제국기(1868–1947)' is an ATLAS historiographic identity label, deliberately not a claim that 大日本帝国 was the formal state title from 1868. The new Meiji government was established in 1868; the Constitution of the Empire of Japan (大日本帝国憲法) was promulgated in 1889; the postwar Constitution of Japan entered into force on 3 May 1947 and transferred sovereignty to the people while making the Emperor a symbol without governing powers.

sources.title: NISHI Amane's Conception of a System of Government
sources.citation_text: The National Diet Library states that the 3 January 1868 Restoration of Imperial Rule established the new Meiji government centered on the imperial court.

sources.title: The Constitution of the Empire of Japan
sources.citation_text: The 1889 Constitution is titled Constitution of the Empire of Japan; Article 1 identifies the Empire of Japan, providing the formal 大日本帝国-era designation evidence.

sources.title: Enactment of the Constitution of Japan
sources.citation_text: The National Diet Library records that the Constitution of Japan came into force on 3 May 1947, the constitutional boundary used by ATLAS between the imperial-era and modern Japan identities.

review_context.decision_authority: User-approved Japan identity re-review on 2026-09-30; current ATLAS rupture rule keeps Yuan/Northern Yuan and other catastrophic state-formations separate despite legal or dynastic continuity.
review_context.identity_note: Stage 1 seed only. Stage 2 must split the existing Emperor Meiji Activity at 3 January 1868, relink 1868–1947 Activities to this identity, split cross-boundary Hirohito and Yoshida Activities at 3 May 1947, preserve sources, remove this seed Activity, and retain current Japan UUID for the post-1947 state. Temporal designation should distinguish the early Meiji Government from the later formal Empire of Japan / 大日本帝国 name.
